forms.detail: EUDA drug profile: white or brown amorphous or crystalline powders, occasionally in capsules, less often tablets; mostly hydrochloride salts; marketed as 'plant food', 'bath salts' or 'research chemicals', often with a printed warning 'not for human consumption'; example brand names Explosion, Blow and Recharge.

DEA bath salts fact sheet: marketed as 'bath salts', 'research chemicals', 'plant food' or 'glass cleaner' and labelled 'not for human consumption'. DEA three-factor analysis (January 2014): powders, crystals, resins, tablets and capsules, also marketed as 'jewelry cleaner', 'stain remover' or 'insect repellants'; typically sold in 50 to 500 mg packets, with bulk quantities from 100 g to over 5 kg.

EUDA khat drug profile: Catha edulis, a flowering evergreen shrub; fresh leaves and shoots, usually supplied as a bundle wrapped in banana leaves; dried leaves; occasionally alcoholic extracts (tinctures); usually imported into Europe by air freight. DEA Diversion Control Division (December 2025): fresh leaves and shoots; dried khat, including 'graba', a dried form produced in Ethiopia; shipped in bundles wrapped in plastic bags or banana leaves.

EMCDDA risk assessment (2011): mainly a white or lightly coloured, typically crystalline powder sold in small sealed bags; also capsules and tablets, some with logo imprints like those on ecstasy tablets, including tablets with a 'captagon' logo seized in Belgium in 2009; 'crystal' samples reported by Austria in 2009.

EMCDDA-Europol joint report: the free base is 'a brown or yellow-green amorphous powder' and the hydrochloride 'a white-tan crystalline hygroscopic powder'; seized as powders, powder-filled capsules, tablets, blotters, liquids and vegetable material; over 200 kg of powder in more than 4 500 cases and about 30 000 tablets in over 500 cases. DEA Diversion Control Division (December 2019): sold as 'bath salt' in 500 mg packets labelled 'for novelty use only' or 'not for human consumption'.

EMCDDA risk assessment (2015): the hydrochloride is a white, crystalline powder; more than 750 kg of powder seized in Europe up to July 2015, the largest single seizure almost 260 kg (Spain, April 2015); 12,400 tablets; smaller amounts of vegetable material, liquids, blotters, capsules and jelly gums; sometimes sold as ecstasy, MDPV or methamphetamine.

EUDA risk assessment (November 2021): typically a powder; tablets and capsules less often; occasionally liquids, herbal material and blotters; both free base and hydrochloride identified. About 2,790 kg of powder seized since 2012 according to the main text (about 2,630 kg in the annex), and a single seizure of just over 120 kg (122 kg in the annex) at the external EU border in 2021, from India.

EUDA risk assessment (November 2021): mainly powder, often white; less often tablets, capsules and liquids (some branded as legal-high type products); occasionally herbal material and blotters; both free base and hydrochloride identified. About 2,720 kg of powder since 2014 in more than 9,000 seizures; for 2021 the main report gives 1,600 kg and the annex and summary 1,400 kg.
EUDA precursor assessment report (February 2026): on the EU market since at least 2014; seizures in the EU close to an average of 300 kilograms per year in 2014-2023.

EUDA initial report (2025): powder in 6,473 of 6,714 cases in 2013-2024 (96.4%), described as white, off-white or yellow; also plant material, liquids, tablets and capsules, and paper; 11,105.399 kg of powder in 2013-2024, about 5,970 kg of it in 2024.

EUDA initial report (2025): powder in 2,314 of 2,397 law-enforcement cases in 2013-2024 (96.5%), typically white or off-white powders or crystals; 45,832 kg of powder in total, 33,207 kg of it in 2024; imports into the Netherlands from India totalled 44,417 kg in 148 imports.

EUDA initial report (2025): mostly powder and, less often, tablets and capsules; 739 of 754 cases in 2011-2024 (98.0%) were powders; 1,069.734 kg of powder in 2011-2024, 1,038.297 kg of it in 2024, about 1.0 tonne of which was imported from India through the Netherlands.

drug_checking.finding: In about 1,500 cases (78.8%) reported by drug checking services, 2-MMC had been sold primarily as 3-MMC; 197 samples in the Netherlands from January to March 2025 had been sold as 3-MMC.
drug_checking.where_when: Europe, to March 2025 (EUDA initial report on 2-MMC, 2025)

drug_checking.finding: Drug checking services reported 11 samples of 4-BMC in 2024 (Austria 1, France 5, Netherlands 1, Spain 4), all powders; of the 10 with purchase information, 8 had been sold as 3-MMC and 2 as 4-MMC. Two samples also contained other substances (one 2-MMC, NEP and 2-CMC; one MDMA). Three more samples (Netherlands, Slovenia) to 14 March 2025, one sold as 3-MMC, and one pill in Switzerland in February 2025.
drug_checking.where_when: Europe, 2024 to March 2025 (EUDA initial report on 4-BMC, 2025)
